6　Eating Exotica

1784年（乾隆四十九年），北京同仁堂药铺来了两位不寻常的顾客。两个年轻人自称琉球国学生，取出一册植物图绘，书中夹着干燥标本。他们逐一请教三位资深药师，帮忙鉴定岛上生长的五十种植物。其师吴继志是一位资深学者，他在信中说明，编纂这册图录及其所收本土物种，是为了让清国专家帮助辨认其中哪些可作药用。这些学生被选中，住在福州指定的馆舍中学习；他们会带着图册拜访当地文士与医者，并把所闻一一记录。在获准游览帝都的那唯一一次行程中，他们在京城唯一接触的对话者便是同仁堂的药师。

In 1784 (Qianlong 49), the Tongrentang pharmacy in Beijing received two unusual customers. Introducing themselves as students from the Ryukyu Kingdom, the two young men produced an album of plant drawings with dried specimens tucked inside. One by one, they asked three leading pharmacists to help them identify fifty plants that grew on their island. A letter from their teacher, a senior scholar named Wu Jizhi, explained that the album and the native species it contained had been compiled so that experts in Qing China could help them identify which ones could be used as medicine. The students, who were selected to study in designated lodges in Fuzhou, would bring the album to local scholars and healers and record whatever they might learn. During the single trip on which they were allowed to tour the imperial capital, the only interlocutors they engaged there were the Tongrentang pharmacists.

八年之后，琉球学者已积累起数册图录，上面批注着与中国专家对谈的记录，此外还有到过琉球的中国商人及其他旅人提供的信息。有时，他们还会随使节另送图画或标本到中国，以确认某种植物的身份。全部往来文字最终汇编为一部图说，书名恰如其分，题为《质问本草》（Shitsumon Honzō，即“本草问题”；见图6.1）。此书在萨摩藩藩主资助下刊行；萨摩藩位于德川日本最南端。事实上，现代学者有充分理由怀疑，图册的编纂与派遣琉球学生赴华，实由萨摩藩的武士医师主持，而“吴继志”其人从未存在。
对萨摩藩精英而言，调查岛上本土植物，是扩大日本在琉球影响的重要一环。日本地缘政治扩张的进程，最终在1879年以吞并琉球、设明治日本的冲绳县而告终。

Eight years later, the Ryukyu scholars had accumulated several albums annotated with records of conversations with Chinese experts, in addition to information supplied by Chinese merchants and other travelers who had visited the island kingdom. On some occasions, additional pictures or specimens were sent with envoys to China in order to ascertain the identity of a plant. The entire set of correspondence was eventually compiled in an illustrated treatise aptly titled
Shitsumon Honzō / Zhiwen bencao (Questions on the subject of Materia Medica

; see figure 6.1). The work was published with the sponsorship of the lord of the Satsuma Domain, the southernmost territory of Tokugawa Japan. In fact, modern scholars have ample grounds to suspect that samurai-physicians in the Satsuma Domain were in fact responsible for making the album and sending the Ryukyu students to China, and there never existed a real person named Wu Jizhi.

For the Satsuma elite, surveying native plants of the islands was an important part of expanding Japanese influence in Ryukyu. The process of Japan’s geopolitical expansion would culminate in the annexation of Ryukyu as Meiji Japan’s Okinawa Prefecture in 1879.
与清廷赞助非医学的博物学、并把药学视为狭窄孤立领域的做法截然不同，本草兼具描述与规范两重面向的整体吸引力，在德川日本兴盛起来。

我们或许会忍不住把近代早期临近结束时中日科学文化的分道扬镳，视为两国在十九世纪后期命运的预兆。但这样做，就可能把两个地方各自的复杂性与能动性化约为民族主义的刻板印象。与晚明士人一样，日本精英武士对本草的兴趣也受到朱熹自然之学的影响。作为将军与藩主的顾问，他们的知识对国内政策的影响力，远大于十八世纪中国的儒者。更重要的是，当时两国在区域与国际贸易中所处的不同位置，促使德川领导层直接干预本土药物资源的开发，以寻找中国进口道地药材的替代品。相比之下，清廷则巧妙地操纵商人，从出口导向的制成品经济中获利，而国家对这一经济领域少有直接监督与了解。
Quite unlike the Qing court’s decision to patronize nonmedical natural history and treat pharmacy as a narrow and isolated field, the holistic appeal of
Honzō / Bencao
, which combined descriptive and prescriptive elements, prospered in Tokugawa Japan.

We may be tempted to see the divergence of scientific cultures of China and Japan toward the end of the early modern era as a harbinger of their fates later in the nineteenth century. Yet to do so risks reducing the complexity and dynamism in each place to nationalistic stereotypes. Like the late Ming literati, the Japanese elite samurais’ pursuit of bencao was also influenced by Zhu Xi’s teaching about nature. As advisors to the Shogun and domainal lords, their knowledge exerted far greater sway on domestic policy than Confucian scholars in eighteenth-century China. More importantly, the different positions of the two countries in regional and international trade at the time prompted Tokugawa leadership to directly intervene in the exploitation of native medicinal resources, in order to find substitutes for authentic materia medica imported from China. In contrast, the Qing state deftly manipulated mercantile agents to profit from an export-oriented economy of manufactured goods, of which the State held little direct supervision and knowledge.

与其把《质问本草》视为清中国错失某种机会的证据，不如用它来揭示一个充满活力的民间知识世界：文士、医者、药师与商人因对新奇之物的好奇而汇聚在一起。同仁堂药师在答复中查阅《本草纲目》及更早的医书，显露出对本行业的一种自豪。
福建的一些医者与学者认为无须知道“野草闲花”的确切身份，另一些人却乐于提供本地药用植物的名称——它们算不上道地，却可作为便宜的替代品。有些人更胆大，愿意尝试新药；另一些人则警告可能的副作用，主张谨慎。
总体而言，清代的答问者愿意逾越社会派定的角色，对从未见过的东西大胆猜测。正是这种好奇心，催生了为新读者重新发明本草的可能。
Rather than seeing
Shitsumon Honzō
as evidence of an opportunity that Qing China failed to pursue, we could instead use the text to reveal a
vernacular
realm of knowledge teeming with scholars, healers, pharmacists, and merchants drawn together by their curiosity about novelties. In their responses, the Tongrentang pharmacists consulted the
Bencao gangmu
and earlier medical sources, demonstrating a certain pride in their trade.
Whereas some physicians and scholars in Fujian saw no need to know the exact identity of “wile grass and idle flower” (
yecao xianhua

), others readily supplied names of local medicinal plants that did not count as daodi authentic but could be useful as cheaper substitutes. Some were more audacious in trying new remedies, while others warned of potential adverse effects and advised caution.

Overall, Qing informants were willing to defy their designated roles in society and venture guesses about something they had never seen before. It was this curiosity that gave rise to the possibility of reinventing bencao for a new audience.
对异域之物癖好的批评，在中国政治传统中源远流长。明代方志编者抨击国家滥用地方土贡，反复告诫不要过高估计“异物”，而应推重“用物”。明代文官接过国家消费与民间消费的二元区分，痛斥皇帝追求浮华享乐、哄抬奢侈品价值的倾向。
但他们同时也在对抗一种大众文化：这种文化不遗余力地传播关于外国土地与异域人物的诱人信息。
到十七世纪中叶清军入关时，精英的奢侈消费与民众的平实日用之间的界线已变得模糊。如果说远方道地药材日益易得，可以指示晚明市场经济渗入日常生活的程度，那么我们便可以从药铺这个制高点，继续观察清代中国消费文化的发展，以及它与更广阔世界的联系。

Critiques of the longing for exotica had a long history in the Chinese political tradition. In their crusade against state abuses of local tribute, Ming gazetteer editors repeatedly warned against the overvaluing of extraordinary things (
yiwu
), praising instead objects of everyday use (
yongwu

). Taking up the binary distinction between state and popular consumption, Ming civil officials railed against the perceived tendency of emperors to pursue frivolous pleasure and inflate the value of luxury goods.
Yet they were also writing against a popular culture that relentlessly spread enticing information about foreign lands and the exotic peoples who lived there.

When the Qing conquest took place in the mid-seventeenth century, the divide between luxury consumption for the elite and plain utility for the populace had become blurred. If the widening availability of daodi medicine from afar is any indicator of the extent to which the market economy penetrated into everyday life in late Ming times, we can continue to observe the development of consumer culture in Qing China from the vantage point of pharmacies, as well as their connection to the wider world.
薛爱华（Edward H. Schafer）在其研究中古中国异物之名著《撒马尔罕的金桃》中指出，截至八世纪中叶的唐代，“进口的时代、交融的时代与黄金时代”同后来由怀旧之情激发的“异域文学兴趣高峰”之间存在鲜明断裂。

换言之，唐代文学中的异域情调，是在异域商品与外国商人退居社会经济生活幕后之后才达到顶峰的。盛清时期的情形则不同：随着指定口岸的海上贸易开放、货物交换加速，文学话语与科学话语也同步共同生产。有时已无法分辨，究竟是现实催生了想象，还是想象催生了现实。对于一个居住在城市中心、可以随时进入市场的人来说，异域之物不只是听说过或读到过的东西，而是可以收集、审视、并且（在许多情况下）吞服的有形标本。本章跟随一位作者穿行于清代货物世界，以揭示本草传统的新方向。章末我将讨论这一民间知识领域的政治意义，以及好奇心的双刃含义。
In his classic study of exotica in medieval China,
The Golden Peaches of Samarkand

, Edward H. Schafer noted the stark disjuncture between the “age of imports, the age of mingling, [and] the golden age” up to the mid-eighth century under the Tang dynasty and a belated “peak of literary interest in the exotic” fueled by nostalgia for that bygone age.

In other words, exoticism in Tang literature peaked only after exotic merchandise and foreign traders receded to the backstage of social and economic life. The situation of High Qing times was different: as the exchange of goods accelerated following the opening of maritime trade in designated ports, so did the coproduction of literary and scientific discourses. At times, it became impossible to tell whether reality led to imagination or the other way around. For someone residing in an urban center with ready access to the marketplace, exotic objects were not just something one might have heard of or read about, but tangible specimens to collect, examine, and (in many cases) ingest. In this chapter, we follow one author’s journey through the Qing world of goods to shed light on new directions in the bencao tradition. Toward the end of the chapter, I will discuss the political significance of this vernacular sphere of knowledge and the double-edged meaning of curiosity.
漂泊一生
A Life Adrift

赵学敏的一生，是十八世纪中国许多读书人的典型。他在杭州人口稠密的城市环境中长大，既无门路也无财富去开启仕途。他受过良好教育，却没有功名，只能在杭州一带为地方官员做家庭教师或私人幕僚之类的临时差事。他与著名藏书家及开业药草师交好，从私家藏书与宴席闲谈中获得了许多知识。年轻时，赵学敏尤其喜爱医术，却从未以医为业。此外，他还自称对烟花、园艺等门类有精深知识，并撰有相关论著，但这些著作生前都未刊行。他的一生与同时代人沈复相似：沈复同样在官场边缘漂泊，并把许多热情倾注于工艺、盆景与园林设计。
由于他们在清代文化场域中处于边缘，其著作生前鲜有人注意，生平也不见于地方志。沈复那部动人的回忆录《浮生六记》，直到他去世数十年后才在苏州的旧货市场上被人发现。同样，赵学敏的生平，也仅因十九世纪身后刊行的著作才为我们所知。

Zhao Xuemin’s life was typical of many educated men in eighteenth-century China. Growing up in the populous urban environment of Hangzhou, Zhao possessed neither connections nor wealth to launch an official career. Well educated but without an examination degree, Zhao took on temporary jobs as family tutor or private secretary to local officials around Hangzhou. He befriended renowned book collectors as well as practicing herbalists, gleaning much information from private libraries and banquet chatter. In his youth, Zhao took a special liking to the art of medicine but never practiced as a physician. In addition, he also claimed deep knowledge in subject matters such as fireworks and horticulture, composing treatises in those fields that were never published in his lifetime. His life resembled that of Shen Fu, a contemporary of his who also lived a peripatetic life at the fringes of officialdom and devoted much passion to crafts, bonsai, and garden design.

Due to their marginal status in the Qing cultural scene, their written works received little notice in their lifetimes, and their lives went unmentioned in local gazetteers. In Shen Fu’s case, his moving memoir,
Six Accounts of a Life Adrift

, only came to be discovered in Suzhou’s flea market decades after his death. Similarly, Zhao Xuemin’s life only became known to us through his writings that were posthumously published in the nineteenth century.

1765年——距赵学敏开始其漫长的幕僚生涯尚有数年——他写了一篇序，纪念一部雄心勃勃的著作完稿，题名《本草纲目拾遗》（以下简称《拾遗》）。预料到读者可能的批评，赵学敏虚构了一段自己与来访者的对话；在这位访客看来，李时珍的《本草纲目》代表着本草之学的顶峰。据访客说，药典传统源自皇家的威望，为此“不惜工费”。他设想当时能够“延天下医流”，考察各地风土习俗。一个普通读书人又怎能把它做得更好呢？对此，赵学敏这样回答：

It was in 1765—a few years before Zhao would embark on a lifetime of temporary employment as a private secretary—that he wrote a preface to mark the completion of an ambitious work he titled
Bencao gangmu shiyi (Supplement to Systematic Materia Medica
, hereafter
Shiyi
). Anticipating possible criticism from readers, Zhao composed a hypothetical dialogue between himself and a visitor, for whom Li Shizhen’s
Bencao gangmu
represented the pinnacle of bencao learning. According to the visitor, the pharmacopeia tradition derived from imperial prestige, for which “no effort and cost were ever spared” (
buxi gongfei
). He imagined that Li Shizhen could “interview physicians from all over the country” and inquire into the various local customs (
tusu
). How could an ordinary scholar go about making it even better? To this question, Zhao Xuemin replied in the following way:

It was in fact imperative, argued Zhao, that his knowledge be recorded at the present moment, lest it might be forever lost to future generations. In the manuscript, Zhao described a total of 921 new drugs in addition to Li Shizhen’s

尽管赵学敏只把自己的本草称为李时珍的“拾遗”，两人的工作方法却大不相同。李时珍精心编排前人权威的引文，把自己的医疗经验层层纳入按语；赵学敏的本草则由一串串当代资料的引文构成，从地方药草师的验方，到清帝国新征服边疆地区的游记，无所不包。1770年代，乾隆帝将一部完整的御纂类书《古今图书集成》赐给杭州一处藏书楼，以酬谢其对《四库全书》工程的慷慨捐助，赵学敏从中急切地采撷了许多新信息。他引用最多的资料之一，是方以智的《物理小识》，以及一位满洲高官在数省任职期间所写的笔记。他的本草传达出清代世界不断扩展的思想与物质视野，以及环绕其间的真切兴奋与困惑。

Although Zhao called his bencao a mere “supplement” to Li Shizhen, their working methods were quite different. Whereas Li Shizhen carefully arranged quotes from previous authorities, subsuming his own medical experience in layers of commentary, Zhao Xuemin’s bencao consisted of strings of quotations from contemporary sources, ranging from local herbalists’ recipes to travelogues from the Qing empire’s newly conquered frontier regions. In the 1770s, the Qianlong emperor bestowed a complete set of the imperial encyclopedia
Gujin tushu jicheng
to a Hangzhou book collection, in return for the latter’s generous donation to the
Siku quanshu
project, and Zhao Xuemin eagerly gleaned much new information from it. Among the sources he quoted most were Fang Yizhi’s
Notes on the Principle of Things

, a high Manchu official’s miscellaneous notes taken during his tenure in many different provinces. His bencao gave voice to the expanding intellectual and material horizons of the Qing world, as well as the verifiable excitement and confusion that surrounded it.
除广泛阅读外，赵学敏还不断为未刊稿本增补札记，直到1803年；材料既来自亲身经历，也来自熟人的见闻。李时珍亲眼看到自己的药典开始刻印，赵学敏却不同：他漫无尽头的探究，使他一步步偏离了最初设定的计划。未完成的稿本最终落入一位本地医者之手，直到1860年代才付印。现在，让我们借赵学敏的眼睛，转向加速跳动的经济交换脉搏如何重塑清代中国的药物物性。

In addition to his broad reading, Zhao continued to add notes to the unpublished manuscript until as late as in 1803, drawing from his personal experiences as well as reports from his acquaintances. Unlike Li Shizhen, who saw his pharmacopeia going to press, Zhao Xuemin’s meandering inquiries led him further and further away from the plan he started with. His unfinished manuscript ended up in a local physician’s possession, and was not published in print until the 1860s. Through Zhao’s eyes, we now turn to the ways in which the quickening pulse of economic exchange reshaped pharmaceutical objecthood in Qing China.
从山野到城镇
From the Mountains, into the Towns
1787年夏，赵学敏在杭州附近的奉化县做事，看见山村人（shancun ren）挑着一捆捆干草到城里市场（chengshi）上出售。他花一百文铜钱买了一捆，觉得它看上去像干薄荷。这种草名叫“六月霜”（liu yue shuang），泡茶极好，还能助消化。赵学敏亲自试服，顿觉暑气消解。

In the summer of 1787, while working in Fenghua County near Hangzhou, Zhao Xuemin saw mountain village people (
shancun ren
) carrying bundles of dried herbs for sale in urban markets (
chengshi
). He bought a bundle with one hundred copper coins, thinking that it looked like dried mint. Named Sixth-Month Frost (
liu yue shuang
), the herb made a very good cup of tea that also improved digestion. Zhao tried it himself and experienced immediate relief from summer heat.

在整部《拾遗》中，赵学敏都敏锐关注这类跨越边界的行为，并记录自己作为消费者，与那些从荒野、帝国边疆和异国“带来”（dailai）新药之人的互动。药材的商业交换绝不限于专营药物的组织与个人。据他所知，福建的板客（ban ke，木材商）常捎带一种远南所产的苦栗，此前本草文献未曾记载，如今却遍布本地药铺，据说是一味良好的泻药，又能治出血。
陕西的羊毛商（yang rong ke）则以拥有一种治疮的流行验方而闻名。
往来于宁波一带沿海港口的洋船，会带来珠儿粉（zhu er fen）之类的新奇食品。
面对“主流”药材早已确立的道地正宗，清代商人常常力图挑战并打破现状：他们宣称自己对新奇药物拥有独特权威，从而开辟新市场。

赵学敏是杭州人，又常往乡间行走，对来自荒野（yesheng）的新产品怀有浓厚兴趣。他认为，自己时代一些最著名的地产药材——例如杭州以西山区於潜县所产的白术——竟不见于李时珍《本草纲目》，实在不可接受。他的调查甚至深入到县以下，直抵采收现场。赵学敏记载，最上等的野生白术出自鹤山；据说那里所产之药“其形有鹤颈鹤头，羽翼足俱全，皮细带黄，切开有朱砂点”。与同时代其他作者相呼应，赵学敏斥责大批栽培白术无用，且可能被肥料污染。他又赶紧补充说，栽培品的根完全不像鹤颈。
家种会使药用植物带上某种“不纯品质”的观念，在此前本草中从未出现；荒野则日益与纯净未染的意象联系在一起。
As a native of Hangzhou and frequent traveler to the countryside, Zhao Xuemin took an avid interest in the new products that came from the wilderness (
yesheng
). He considered it unacceptable that some of the most famous regional varieties in his lifetime, such as
Bai Zhu
from Yuqian County— a mountainous region west of Hangzhou—received no mention in Li Shizhen’s
Bencao gangmu

. His investigation even went below the county level and reached the sites of harvest. The most superior kind of wild Bai Zhu, noted Zhao, came from Crane Hill, a place where the herb allegedly “has [the] long neck, wings and claws of a crane; the skin is thin with yellow hues. If you cut it open, there are vermillion-colored dots in the texture.” Echoing other contemporary authors, Zhao Xuemin dismissed the bulk supply of cultivated Bai Zhu as useless and possibly contaminated with fertilizers. He hastened to add that the roots of cultivated herbs looked nothing like the neck of a crane.

The notion that domestic cultivation would somehow impart an “impure quality” to a medicinal plant was unseen in previous bencao, and wilderness came to be increasingly associated with the image of the pure and pristine.

对荒野的迷恋没有止境。赵学敏很快发现，於潜白术的商业成功迅速耗尽了当地的野生白术资源，反过来又刺激人们去开发别处的同类植物。1791年，一位访客送给赵学敏一批青田县所产的天然生成（tian sheng）白术；青田在沿海更南处，靠近浙闽边界。他听说，这种新采之药并不长在土里，而是长在某处岩崖表面；每年只能获得二三十斤。他注意到，干燥的根也有优雅的弧线，形似鹤颈，这一令人喜爱的特征让他想起鹤山。远近其他来源的野生白术标本也送到他手中；赵学敏会剖开它们，审视纹理与颜色，并记录味道。杭州附近出产的一种野术“气味香甜”，据说生嚼可以生津、解渴、醒脾。重要的是，野生白术成了买不起人参之人的首选补药。

Fascination with the wild knew no end. Zhao soon found out that the commercial success of the Yuqian variety had quickly exhausted the sources of wild Bai Zhu there and, in turn, incentivized the exploitation of similar plants elsewhere. In 1791, a visitor gave Zhao a batch of natural grown (
tian sheng

) Bai Zhu from Qingtian County, a place further south down the coast near the border between Zhejiang and Fujian. He was told that this freshly harvested herb grew not in soil, but on the surface of a particular rocky cliff; only 20–30 jin of the plant was made available every year. He noted that the dried root also had an elegant curve resembling a crane’s neck, a desirable feature that reminded him of Crane Hill. Samples of wild Bai Zhu reached him from other sources near and far, and Zhao would cut them open, gaze at their texture and color, and record their taste. One especially successful variety found near Hangzhou was marketed as “fragrant and sweet” and recommended for casual chewing in order to alleviate thirst and aid digestion. Importantly, wild Bai Zhu became a choice tonic for those who could not afford ginseng.

从消费者的角度看，追求纯正地道的产品，未必妨碍人们享受激烈竞争所带来的丰富选择。化州地处两广交界，所产橘红向来被视为这一药物的道地正品。赵学敏听说，州衙门前一棵老树所结的橘子尤其为人珍视。由于此树每月只结“一果”，替代品与假货便充斥市场。赵学敏引用一位当代药草师的建议，描述如何凭外观辨认真正的化州橘红。与此同时，他也乐于记载：杭州家附近的一座市镇，近来开始出售一种新式的甜橘红。赵学敏指出，它味道宜人，不如化州橘红辛辣，或许更适合娇弱的南方人。

From a consumer’s perspective, the pursuit of pure, authentic products did not necessarily prevent one from delighting in the wide range of options made available by intense competition. Blood orange peels (
juhong

) from Huazhou, a place located at the border between Guangdong and Guangxi, had long been considered to be the daodi authentic variety of this cooling drug. Zhao Xuemin heard that oranges growing on one old tree in front of the prefectural government office were especially coveted. Since the tree only grew “one fruit per month,” substitutes and fakes flooded the market. Quoting a contemporary herbalist’s recommendation, Zhao described visual cues to tell the authentic Huazhou orange peels from others. At the same time, he was also delighted to report that a market town near his home in Hangzhou had recently begun to sell a new variety of sweet orange jam. Pleasant to taste and less pungent than the Huazhou variety, noted Zhao, it might be more suitable for delicate southerners.

十八世纪中国最有名的替代药物，无疑是日益流行的东洋参与西洋参。
然而在这些产品到来之前，像赵学敏这样的清代消费者，早已在品尝国内出产的各种“类人参”产品。在《拾遗》中，赵学敏记述了昭通府（滇黔交界）、广西右江、琼州府（海南岛）、西藏以及“广西山峒”等地所产类人参药材。
他断定，其中许多产品其实与最昂贵的朝鲜参、辽东参大不相同。更令他难以接受的是，一些商帮公然把本地草药当作“人参”出售。例如，福建商人从“红毛”番人那里带来一种不知名的植物，“绝不类参”。
沿海的福建省如今也有了自己的本地“人参”品种，随后又被引种到河南，很可能是由往来两省的商人带去的。《拾遗》转引张觐斋等人的评论，认为如今几乎到处都声称有“土”产人参，且“人亦日搜奇”，到“穷岩荒壑”中寻找相似草根充作替代品。
问题在于，没有人能确切说出一种新产品的药效。

He concluded that many of these products were, in fact, quite different from the most expensive Korean and Liaodong ginseng. Less palatable for him was the blatant attempt by some merchant groups to sell their local herbs as “ginseng.” For instance, Fujian merchants brought an unknown plant from the “red-haired” (

The coastal province Fujian now had its own local variety of “ginseng,” which in turn was transplanted to Henan, probably carried by merchants moving between the two provinces. Zhao complained that virtually everywhere now claimed to have a “local” (
tu

) variety of ginseng. “Day in and day out, people search for curiosities,” wrote Zhao, to the extent that they would comb through “remote rocks and barren valleys” looking for any obscure herb, hoping to earn some profit by selling it as a cheaper substitute.
The problem was that no one could speak with certainty for a novel product’s medicinal efficacy.

宋代药典最早以贬义使用“野生”一词：编者告诫，野生胡麻、蒜、茄、莴苣等植物应慎用，因为与更可靠的栽培品种相比，它们可能有毒。
十六世纪的本草作者，如李时珍与陈嘉谟，进一步告诫医者要区分植物的“野生”与“家种”类型。李时珍写道，野生山药（shuyu）常作药用，家种山药药力较弱，更适合当食物吃。
陈嘉谟在其节要本草中告诫，临证不可把同一药物不同来源的品种混用，并作了一首歌诀让弟子记诵。
总体而言，李、陈二人都关注同一植物“野生”与“栽培”品种的不同品质，却并未明确偏好其中一种。
The Song pharmacopeia first used the term “wild grown” (
yesheng
) in a negative light: the editors warned that plants such as
wild
sesame, garlic, eggplant, and lettuce should be used with caution, as they might be poisonous compared with the more reliable domesticated varieties.
Sixteenth-century bencao authors such as Li Shizhen and Chen Jiamo further admonished physicians to distinguish “wild” from “homegrown” types of plants. Li Shizhen wrote that while wild yam (
shuyu
) was used regularly as a medicine, homegrown yam had less potency and was better eaten as food.
Chen Jiamo in his abridged bencao warned against mixing different sources of the same herb in one’s practice and composed a rhyme on this topic for his disciples to memorize.
In general, both Li and Chen were interested in the different qualities of “wild” and “cultivated” varieties of the same plant, yet held no clear preference for one over the other.
然而，十七世纪出现了对“野生”药用植物的显著兴趣。杭州人卢之颐看不上城中随处可见的梅树，主张采梅实应取“野生，及未经就接者”。
苏州人张璐以本地所产罗勒等香草为傲，对常见药材白术也有一番见解。张璐指出，店铺中常见的品种“皆栽灌而成，故其气浊”，不如“于潜野生者气清”。
江南医者吴仪洛（约1704—1766）自称在“从新”的同时更新汪昂的畅销本草，他也抱怨店铺所售乌头的品质：

Lu Zhiyi, a native of Hangzhou, dismissed the ubiquitous plum trees planted around the city and recommended harvesting plum fruits instead from “the wild-grown trees, or those whose branches had not yet been grafted.”
Zhang Lu, a Suzhou native proud of locally produced basil and other fragrant herbs, was also opinionated about the common medicinal plant Bai Zhu. The “cultivated and irrigated” (
zaiguan
) varieties commonly seen in shops, noted Zhang, were inferior to a new variety “grown in the wilderness,” which possessed “purer

),” complained about the quality of aconite sold in shops:
从前附子皆野生，所产甚罕，价值甚高，而力甚大。近今俱是种者，出产多而价值贱，力甚薄。土人以盐腌之，愈减其力。

Recently, it has come to be cultivated; the harvest is more abundant, but the price has dropped and its power has become quite thin. Local people preserve it with salt, which further weakens it.

吴仪洛的抱怨，反映出他那个时代跨区域贸易的实质扩张，以及供应增加所引发的心理效应。这种偏好野生、轻视家种的新风气，若让不到两个世纪前的李时珍与陈嘉谟看到，定会感到错愕。

Wu Yiluo’s complaint reflected the substantive expansion of interregional trade in his own times and the psychological effect elicited by increased supply. This new preference for the wild over the homegrown would have startled Li Shizhen and Chen Jiamo less than two centuries earlier.
荒野的驯化
The Taming of Wilderness
然而，从荒野“带来”新药的过程，绝非平和而无张力。《拾遗》及其所引资料的一个耐人寻味之处，是它们显然乐于铺陈获取异域之物所必需的艰险、暴力与人心机巧。赵学敏在浙江沿海游历时得知，仙居县有人组成专业的山间采集队，专在高崖陡岩上采摘娇嫩的菌类。这些人带着专门工具，开始登山前还要举行自己的仪式；每年都有人死在这桩危险而有利可图的生意中。
在广西别处，人们发现了一种罕见的“金果榄”树，原本生长在越南北部。赵学敏的父亲曾得到二十枚这种珍贵的果实，由土人（turen）从深谷谷底采来。
人们冒着生命危险获取这些产品，这本身就抬高了它们的市场价值与人们所相信的药效。
The process of “bringing over” new medicines from the wilderness, however, was by no means peaceful and free of tension. One intriguing feature of
Shiyi

and the sources it cited was a conspicuous willingness to elaborate on the danger, violence, and human cunning that were necessary to obtain exotica. When traveling along the Zhejiang coast, Zhao Xuemin learned that people from Xianju County had formed a group of professional mountain foragers, who specialized in picking delicate fungi from steep rocks on high cliffs. Carrying their special tools, the company performed their own rituals upon beginning their ascent up the mountains; every year, someone would die from this risky yet lucrative trade.
Elsewhere in Guangxi Province, people discovered a rare kind of “golden fruit olive” (
jin guo lan
) tree, which was originally grown in northern Vietnam. Zhao’s father once obtained twenty pieces of the precious fruit, which was picked by local people (
turen
) from the bottom of deep valleys.
The fact that people risked their lives to obtain these products only served to increase their market value and perceived efficacy.
1790年冬，一个名叫李金什的男子在临安县西门外的肉铺前停下，看屠夫剖开一只羊的胃。羊内脏中滚出一个奇怪的东西；它看上去“如鸭卵黄，匀圆光洁，浮水盆上”。屠夫认出这是“百草丹”，并告诉李，自己从事屠宰三十多年，只见过三次这种东西。李金什大感兴趣，从屠夫手中买下此物，带到赵学敏那里；赵学敏当时正住在附近做私人幕僚。两人一同察看，并与牛黄相比较。

In the winter of 1790, a man named Li Jinshi stopped by a butcher shop outside the Western gate of Lin’an County and watched the butcher cut open the stomach of a goat. A strange object emerged from the goat’s viscera; it looked “like duck egg yolk, perfectly round, shiny and smooth, when put in a basin of water it would float.” The butcher identified it as “hundred-herb elixir” (
baicao dan

) and told Li that he had only seen such a thing three times in more than thirty years of his practice. Intrigued, Li purchased the object from the butcher and brought it to Zhao Xuemin, who was then living in the vicinity as a private secretary. Together they examined it and compared it with ox bezoars.
赵学敏另有四次提到同一个李金什，说他是山东半岛北岸蓬莱县人。赵从李那里听到当地渔民猎捕海狗（haigou，“海中之犬”）的生动故事。据李说，要杀这些敏捷的动物，唯一的机会是一年中最冷的月份：河口封冻，许多海狗从深海浮出，躺在冰上晒太阳。这时，骤入水，以木棍击其腰，方可得之。若冰裂或步履有声，非其睡时，皆不可得。然每年打狗堕水溺死者亦多，因利重，人亦不惜躯命以往。

On four other occasions, Zhao identified the same Li Jinshi as a man from Penglai, a county that sits at the northern coast of the Shandong peninsula. From him, Zhao heard vivid tales of how local fishermen hunted for seals (
haigou

, “sea dogs”). According to Li, the only opportunity to kill these agile creatures would be during the coldest months of the year, when river mouths were frozen, and many sea dogs emerged from the deep sea to lie on the ice, bathing under the sun. And then, [hunters] quickly jump into the water, hit the seadog’s waist with a wooden stick, and only in that way can they get it. Otherwise, if the ice cracks, or one makes the slightest sound with footsteps, or if the seadogs are not asleep, it would be impossible. But every year many people are drowned to death while “hitting the dogs.” As the profit is high, they are willing to risk their lives.
海狗脂肪尤其引起赵学敏的兴趣。他听说沿海居民把几滴这种珍贵的油脂滴入海中，浑浊的海水顿时被照亮，藏在深处的鲍鱼与海参都显露出来。有人还把海狗脂“从关东”带给赵学敏——那本是普通商人不得进入的满洲故地。赵学敏察看此物，形容它“绿色如干糊”。得知当地人用它作治冻疮的油膏，他断定这证明了这种神秘药物的“热烈”之性。

The body fat of sea dogs was of special interest to Zhao Xuemin. He had seen coastal residents put a few drops of the precious liquid into the sea, which instantly illuminated the turbid water, revealing eels and sea cucumbers that hid in the depths. Someone had also brought some sea dog fat to Zhao “from East of the Pass”—that is, the Manchu homeland that ordinary traders should have been forbidden to enter. Examining the substance, Zhao described it as a “dry, greenish paste.” Learning that locals used it as an ointment for cold sores, Zhao concluded that this proved the “hot and fierce” (
re lie
) nature of this mysterious cure.

这类猎捕故事大量出现，给赵学敏留下深刻印象，他把它们写入《拾遗》。他的一位学生曾向他讲述浙东山区猎捕大乌鸦的事。同样，这种鸟因其胆汁据称有药效而成了“土人”觊觎的对象。按猎人的说法，此鸟的胆囊白天总是空的，夜里则充满胆汁。猎人会耐心等到乌鸦睡熟，迅速用快刀剖开它的腹部，完整取出胆囊，不洒一滴。
虎肉是著名药物，据说能预防天花，于是猎人会放出一条野狗，诱虎捕杀；据说这样一来，老虎便“醉”了，无法逃走。猎人循着狗血的踪迹，捉住动弹不得的老虎，取肉、脂、骨入药。
自张璐十七世纪的本草著作把鹿胎（lu tai）列为强效药（李时珍《本草纲目》未提及）之后，猎人便开始追逐幼鹿与怀孕的母鹿。
动物药在本草传统中历来占有稳固位置，但此前从未有如此多描写人们如何诱骗、制服、然后杀死动物的生动记述进入这一文体。那些故事似乎把人的机巧本身也当作药物效力的一部分来颂扬。
An abundance of such hunting stories made such a lasting impression on Zhao Xuemin that he recorded them in
Shiyi

. A student of his once told him about the hunting of large ravens that lived in the mountains of eastern Zhejiang. Again, the birds became desirable to “local people” because of the alleged medicinal virtues of their bile. According to hunters’ lore, the bird’s gallbladder was always empty during the day and full of bile at night. Hunters would wait patiently until a raven fell asleep, quickly cut open its abdomen with a sharp knife, and snatch the gallbladder intact with no liquid spilled.

Tiger meat was a famous remedy said to be able to prevent smallpox, and so hunters would release a stray dog and entice a tiger to kill it, which allegedly made the tiger “drunk” and unable to flee. Following the trail of dog blood, they would capture the immobile tiger, harvesting its meat, fat, and bones for medicinal use.
Ever since deer fetus (
lu tai
) came to be mentioned as a powerful remedy in Zhang Lu’s seventeenth-century bencao treatise (Li Shizhen said nothing about it in
Bencao gangmu
), hunters began to go after fawns and pregnant does.

Although animal drugs had always held a secure place in the bencao tradition, never before had so many vivid depictions of people tricking, subjugating, and then killing animals found their way into the genre. Those stories seemed to celebrate human cunning itself as part of the efficacy for those medicines.
动物来源的异域药物一旦从荒野“带来”、变成可消费之物，便留在寻常人家手中，引发更多好奇与敬畏。赵学敏曾认识一个叫王沂堂的人，家中铁盒里藏着一块“狮粪”。他用碎铁“养”它，此物便硬如金属，磨起来会呈红色（大概是铁锈所致）。王告诉赵学敏，这是治疗下体恶疮、去疮痂的良药。
1796年，赵的另一位姓邵的朋友得到少量“狮脂”，据说是治泌尿疾病的药。邵拿不准该不该试用这种异域药物，便把它送给一位同乡，同乡又高价转卖给第三人。买主服下“半黍许”此物，夜半而死。中间卖主害怕官府查究，也自尽了。然而，这样的惨剧并没有让赵学敏怀疑药物本身的效力，反而使他断定，狮脂的药力对人体肠胃来说大概“过于酷烈”。

Once “brought over” from the wilderness and transformed into consumable objects, exotic drugs of animal origin remained in the possession of common households, eliciting further curiosity and awe. Zhao Xuemin once knew a man named Wang Yitang, who kept a piece of “lion feces” at home in an iron box. Nourished (
yang
) with bits of iron, the substance became hard as metal, and developed a reddish hue (probably from iron rust). Wang told Zhao that this made an excellent remedy for malignant sores (
e chuang
) on the lower body and the removal of scabs.

In 1796, another friend of Zhao surnamed Shao obtained a small amount of “lion fat,” a purported remedy for urological dysfunctions. Uncertain about whether he should try the exotic drug or not, Shao gave it to a townsman, who then sold it on to a third person for a high price. That night, the buyer took one “half kernel” of the substance and was found dead in the morning. Fearing an official investigation, the intermediary seller also killed himself. Tragic stories like this, however, did not lead Zhao to question the efficacy of the drug itself, but rather to conclude that the potency of lion fat was probably “too harsh” for human bowels.

屠夫、渔夫与猎海狗的人，都懂得剖开动物身体是什么滋味，也懂得维持这样一份生计需要多少辛劳与机巧。
Butchers, fishermen, and seal hunters knew what it was like to cut open an animal’s body, and the toil and cunning required to maintain such a livelihood.

真正值得注意的是，赵学敏这样一位受过教育、温文尔雅的士人，竟悉心采访这些行商工匠，并在自己的本草中承认他们的权威。在这一传递过程中，这类故事成为清代消费者所理解的“荒野”的有机组成部分，激发他们对获取这些标本的异域之地的想象。荒野并非空无一物的空间，而是栖息着“凶猛”的生物，以及冒着生命危险猎捕它们的、富于进取心的“土人”。赵学敏讲述这些故事的方式里，带着一种冷酷的快意。用马蒂娜·西伯特（Martina Siebert）的话说，这里的动物不是考据家们在纸上津津乐道的“文本动物”。
它们也不是理学家笔下用来阐明人性潜能与局限的寓言动物。它们凶猛的外形，反而激起人类征服、占有、并（如果可能）吞食它们的欲望。

What is truly remarkable is that Zhao Xuemin, an educated and urbane literatus, took great care to interview these tradesmen and acknowledged their authority in his bencao. In this process of transmission, these kinds of stories became an organic part of what wilderness meant to Qing consumers, fueling their fantasy about the exotic places where such specimens were procured. The wilderness was no empty space but was populated with “fierce” creatures, as well as the enterprising “local people” who risked their lives to hunt them. There was a sense of ruthless pleasure in the ways in which Zhao Xuemin related these stories. The animals here were not, in Martina Siebert’s words, the “text animals” that philologists joyously pursued on paper.

Neither were they allegorical animals like those which appeared in the writings of neo-Confucian teachers to illuminate the potential and limitations of human nature. Their fierce appearances instead elicited human desire to subjugate them, possess them, and (if possible) consume them.
深入荒野的商业活动，大多避开了官方的注意；地方志中常见的抱怨只是说，穷民（qiongmin）逐利会迅速耗尽一地的自然资源。晚明官员尚可呈请将地方土贡负担折变，清代知县却几乎没有权力去对付远远超出其辖区范围的商业活动。
直到白莲教大起义之后，清朝官员才注意到所谓陕、川、豫三省交界地带大片蔓延的药材种植场（chang）。严如熤（1759—1826）原为私人幕僚，因对叛乱地区了解深切而最终升迁入仕；他报告说，黄连与厚朴是商人竞相种植、运销远方（xingyuan）的两种最著名的道地药材。与流俗之见相反，严如熤指出，这些药其实都种在深山之中：

The commercial operations that extended far into the wilderness had largely evaded official attention, except for the common complaints in local gazetteers that the drive for profit among desperate people (
qiongmin

) would quickly exhaust the natural resources of a place. Whereas late Ming officials could petition for the conversion of local tribute burdens, Qing magistrates wielded little power with which to confront commercial operations that extended far beyond their jurisdiction.
It was only in the aftermath of the Great White Lotus Rebellion that Qing officials paid attention to the sprawling plantations (
chang

) of medicinal plants in the so-called tri-province area between Shaanxi, Sichuan, and Henan. Yan Ruyu (1759–1826), a former private secretary who eventually rose up the official ranks owing to his deep knowledge of the rebellious region, reported that Golden Thread and magnolia barks (
houpu
) were two of the most famous daodi authentic medicines that merchants sought to cultivate and sell to faraway places (
xingyuan
). Contrary to popular belief, Yan pointed out that these drugs were, in fact, all cultivated in the deep mountains:
老林久辟，厚朴、黄连之野生者绝少。厚朴树则系栽成于小坡平坝，中有笔筒厚朴，言其小也。树至数年、十数年如杯如碗，则好厚朴矣。黄连于既辟老林山凹山沟中栽种，商人写地数十里遍栽之，须十年方成。常年佃棚户守连，一厂辄数十家。大抵山愈高，谷愈深，则所产更好。

The ancient woodlands having been cleared long ago, the Golden Thread and Magnolia barks that are produced here are hardly wild. Magnolia saplings are planted on plain slopes and patchy terrain, and they are as thin as a brush pot. The trees grow to the diameter of a cup or a bowl in several to a dozen years, and they then yield good quality bark. As for Golden Thread, it is cultivated in the hollows and valleys of cleared mountain land. Merchants buy an enclosure with a circumference of several tens of
li
, and plant the herb all over. Since it takes up to ten years for the plant to grow, they rent the land to “shed people” (
pengmin
) to take care of the herbs, and on each yard there are several dozen households. In general, the quality of medicine is the best when the mountain is high and the valley is deep.
Editor's note (Chinese): 此段据《三省边防备览》卷九所见数字文本恢复；原文“佃棚户守连”的具体契约关系，不能仅凭此句确定为商人将土地出租给棚户。个别字形及作者所据9:15b原页仍待核对。
严如熤的敏锐观察，揭示了“野生”与“家种”这类范畴在清代商业行话中可疑的地位，因为标为“野生”的植物，很可能就是人工栽培的。严如熤对“棚民”工具性角色的敏感，在某种意义上可与赵学敏对商人与猎人的细致观察相比。两人虽然都以读书人身份长大，却无法过一种脱离实务的生活。相反，他们置身于官府非正式的幕僚队伍中，为了生存，不得不关注三教九流。

Yan Ruyu’s astute observation reveals the dubious status of categories like “wild” and “homegrown” in Qing commercial parlance, for the plants labeled “wild” may well have been grown artificially. Yan Ruyu’s sensitivity to the instrumental role of “shed people” is, in a sense, comparable to Zhao Xuemin’s close observation of traders and hunters. Despite their upbringing as educated men, they could not live a life aloof from practical concerns. Instead, their placement among the informal retinue of government compelled them to pay attention to different walks of life in order to survive.
庖厨之变
Culinary Transformations
新药被捕获、驯化之后，往往还需要进一步的技术才能制成可服用之物。在这方面，此前的本草文献几乎无从指导，制药与烹饪的界线很快变得模糊。由于异域食材往往难以嵌入旧有的药方，它们更常被纳入家常做饭的日常流程。

Captured and tamed, new remedies often required further expertise in order to prepare them for consumption. In this regard, little guidance could be found in previous bencao literature, and the division between pharmaceutical and culinary processes quickly became blurred. Since exotic ingredients often could not fit easily into previously used medicinal formulas, they were more frequently folded into the regular course of preparing a meal at home.
清代作者在既有食养本草文献的基础上，努力对付这些新食材，并尽可能形成共识。西洋参性寒，东洋参则没那么寒。过甜则壅滞，过热则生痰。凡是论述药性，几乎总伴随着缓和其副作用的方法：例如，性凉的西洋参可以用米饭蒸制，使其变得温和可口。
西藏的灵药“冬虫夏草”被认为是温性，在若干食疗方中与凉性的鸭肉搭配，药气“直贯鸭全身，无不透浃”，制成滋养病后体虚者的食物。
其他常与药材一同烹制的流行“底料”还包括鸡肉与动物内脏——可以说，这些才往往是菜肴的主要滋养所在。
于是，吃与烹成为清代消费者的实验场：以此获得的经验，一旦以固定程式表述出来，便会被算作可与他人分享的有效知识。
编者说明：《本草纲目拾遗·夏草冬虫》所见炖老鸭法作“其药气能从头中直贯鸭全身，无不透浃”，说的是药气而非蒸汽；所见文本亦汇录了药性与用法不同的诸家说法。作者所据版本原页待核。

Building on previous literatures on dietetic bencao, Qing authors grappled with the new ingredients and tried to form a consensus wherever possible. American ginseng was cold in nature; Japanese ginseng less so. Too much sweetness caused congestion, and excessive heat generated phlegm. Statements about the nature of drugs were almost always accompanied by methods of moderating their pernicious effects: the cool-natured American ginseng, for instance, could be rendered mild and agreeable by steaming it over rice.

The Tibetan wonder drug “Summer herb, winter worm,” which was held to be warm in nature, was paired in several recipes with cool-natured duck meat, steamed “through the entire body of the bird” to make a nourishing food for convalescing patients.

Other popular “base” ingredients that were often prepared together with medicinal ingredients included chicken and animal viscera, which arguably might well have been the principal nourishments of the dish.
Eating and cooking thus became sites of
experimentation
for Qing consumers, in the sense that
experience
gathered this way, and articulated in a formulaic fashion, would then be counted as valid information to share with others.
Editor's note (Chinese): 《本草纲目拾遗·夏草冬虫》所见炖老鸭法作“其药气能从头中直贯鸭全身，无不透浃”，说的是药气而非蒸汽；所见文本亦汇录了药性与用法不同的诸家说法。作者所据版本原页待核。
日本学者筱田统（Shinoda Osamu）认为“饮食生活的现代化”（shokuseika ni okeru kindaika）发生在明清之际，这是很有道理的。
十六世纪晚期，李时珍记载鱼翅味道佳美，却未评论其药效；两百年后，鱼翅已成为宴席上的“常嗜之品”，赵学敏引用《闽部食疏》等资料，称它能“长腰力”。
数十种记载描述了“燕窝”这一珍馐，却对其本来面目众说纷纭。燕子长什么样？吃的是什么？有人说是小鱼，有人说是粉状的岩盐，有人说是小贝类。至于如何烹制上宴，也有分歧：有人主张加糖甜食，有人斥责不应把它做成甜品。
值得注意的是，鱼翅与燕窝本质上都是晚明南海与东南亚海上贸易的副产品；在这些地区，捕鲨变得更加普遍。对沿海生境的开发，催生了从岩崖采集燕窝这一专门而高风险的行业。两种食材又都被认为具有“开胃”的药效。换言之，食用这些食物，促进了更多的食用。
编者说明：《本草纲目拾遗·沙鱼翅》所见文本称鱼翅为“常嗜之品”，并引《闽部食疏》“长腰力”；作者所据版本原页待核。
The Japanese scholar Shinoda Osamu is quite right to suggest that the “modernization of dietetic life” (
shokuseika ni okeru kindaika
) took place across the Ming-Qing transition.

In the late sixteenth century, Li Shizhen noted the good taste of shark fin, but made no comment on its medicinal virtues; two hundred years later, it had become a “regular favorite” of banquets, and Zhao Xuemin quoted multiple sources recommending it for “enhancing core strength” (
zhang yao li
Dozens of accounts described the delicacy known as “swallow’s nest” (
yanwo

) but disagreed over its true nature. What did the swallows look like? What kind of food did they eat? Some said small fish, some said powdery rock salt, some said small shellfish. There was also disagreement over how to prepare it for banquet: some recommended it sweetened, some scolded against eating it as a dessert.

Notably, both shark fin and swallow’s nest were essentially by-products of the late Ming maritime trade into the South China Sea and Southeast Asian countries, where the hunting of sharks became more prevalent. The exploitation of the coastal habitat in these regions gave rise to the specialized, highly risky trade of collecting swallow’s nests from rocky cliffs. Both substances were also recommended as possessing the medicinal virtue of “opening up the appetite” (
kai wei
). The consumption of these foods, in other words, facilitated yet more consumption.
Editor's note (Chinese): 《本草纲目拾遗·沙鱼翅》所见文本称鱼翅为“常嗜之品”，并引《闽部食疏》“长腰力”；作者所据版本原页待核。
吃不熟悉的东西而中毒相当常见，赵学敏便收集熟人的亲身证言，以判断某种植物是否可以安全食用。一位姓周的朋友告诉他，自己曾不慎吃下色彩艳丽的秋海棠花——据说此花有毒——结果惊恐了一整夜。到天亮时发现自己呼吸如常，周便断定此物的有毒之名必定是假的。
在另一则亲身故事中，赵学敏回忆家中一名年轻仆役患慢性间歇热多年。有一天，他“偶食辣酱”，此后再未发病。
赵学敏指出，从没有人提到过这种流行调味品的抗疟功效。在缺乏权威意见的情况下，他收集了两百多人的传闻证言，其中许多人是像他一样的私人塾师。
编者说明：《本草纲目拾遗·辣茄》所见文本称小仆秋天发疟，迁延至初冬，偶食辣酱后每餐食之，又用以煎粥，未几自愈；英文底本称患病多年，所见原文并无此说。作者所据版本原页仍待核。

Poisoning from eating unfamiliar foods was quite common, and Zhao collected personal testimonies from his acquaintances to ascertain whether a plant was safe to eat. A friend named Zhou told him about a night spent in panic, after carelessly consuming the colorful flower of autumn crabapple (
qiuhaitang
), which was supposed to be toxic. When he found himself still breathing normally at daybreak, Zhou concluded that the poisonous reputation of the plant must have been false.

In another personal story, Zhao Xuemin recalled a young servant of their household, who had suffered from chronic intermittent fever for many years. One day, he “accidentally ate chili pepper sauce” and never lapsed back into fever again.

No one had mentioned the antimalarial properties of the popular condiment, noted Zhao. In the absence of an authoritative opinion, he gathered anecdotal testimonies from over two hundred individuals, many of whom were private tutors like him.

我们或可回想，晚明涉猎食养本草的名士陈继儒曾宣称，日常饮食之事可以自己作主。在劝人节制、斥责饕餮的悠久食养论著传统中，陈继儒打趣说，读本草让他舌头发动，也提醒自己要节制口腹之欲。然而，赵学敏及其十八世纪资料探究食物与药物的种种方式，并不那么强调事物的固有属性，而更看重烹饪方法如何使异域之物变得可食、有益，甚至令人愉悦。赵学敏满怀欣赏地记下与同僚共餐时遇到的新奇美味。1788至1791年间，他在临安为刘知县做事；刘知县是高官、著名学者刘墉（1719—1805）的侄子。在一次县衙宴席上，赵学敏尝到一种从未见过的鲜美蛤蜊，是刚从刘知县北方沿海的家乡送来的。
他提到扬州富裕盐商摆下的豪宴，总是以鱼翅、燕窝羹和大量野味开场。
赵学敏显然熟悉旧本草中反对过度饮食的告诫，但在整部《拾遗》中，他对制药与烹饪程序的混同少有异议。相反，人们能在多大程度上为自身利益而操纵自然，显然令他感到愉悦。

We might recall how Chen Jiru, the celebrity author who dabbled in late Ming dietetic bencao, announced that the matter of everyday eating and drinking was “something that I could govern myself.” Writing in the long tradition of dietetic treatises that advised temperance and decried gluttony, Chen joked that reading the bencao made him waggle his tongue and remember to restrain his appetite. The various ways in which Zhao Xuemin and his eighteenth-century sources explored food and medicine, however, placed less emphasis on the innate properties of things than on how culinary methods might render exotic substances edible, wholesome, and even pleasant. Zhao wrote with appreciation about the new delicacies he encountered at shared meals with his colleagues. From 1788 to 1791, Zhao worked in Lin’an for Magistrate Liu, nephew of the high official and renowned scholar Liu Yong (1719–1805). At one of the magistrate’s banquets, Zhao tasted a delicious clam that he had never seen before, which had been delivered fresh from Liu’s hometown on the northern coast.
He referred to the sumptuous parties offered by the wealthy salt merchants of Yangzhou, which always started with shark fins, swallow’s nest stews, and lavish amounts of wild game.
While Zhao was clearly familiar with the admonition against excessive consumption in older bencao, throughout
Shiyi
he voiced little protest against the conflation of medicinal and culinary procedures. Rather, he took obvious pleasure in the extent to which people could manipulate nature for their own benefit.

这种操纵倾向有一组相当极端的例子，竟以其他活物作为制药的工具。赵学敏写到一位名叫朱秋亭的人，花“千金”从商人手中买来一个秘方，能把一种极苦的草药制成道地辽东人参的满意替代品。赵学敏恳求朱秋亭的弟弟，才得知做法：取珠参五钱，切片，与附子末三分拌匀。取鸡蛋一枚，去掉蛋清蛋黄，把五钱参片装入蛋壳，封口，让母鸡孵。等小鸡孵出后，取出药蛋，在壳上画一圈作记号；如此反复七次，共画七圈，药便制成。据说它能代替辽参。
另一位朋友提供了类似的人工制造（rengong zhizao）法。此法诱使野鹤孵化煮熟的蛋，重复三次，再用蛋壳作饮器，据称有多种保健功效。赵学敏说，这罕见的物件在当地市场能卖到很高的价钱。
两例都相信，与母鸟身体的亲密接触会把神奇药效注入苦涩无生气的东西之中。

One rather extreme set of examples of this manipulative tendency mobilizes other living creatures as the instruments of pharmaceutical processing. Zhao Xuemin wrote about a man named Zhu Qiuting, who spent “a thousand taels of silver” to buy a secret recipe from traders to prepare a very bitter herb into a satisfactory substitute for authentic Liaodong ginseng. He shared it with Zhao Xuemin begrudgingly: Take five ounces of the bitter herb, mix and rub with powdered aconite. Find a fresh egg, empty the egg white and yolk, put five ounces of the herbal mixture into the shell, and seal it back intact. Let a hen sit on the fake “egg” (marked with a circle) along with her other eggs. When the latter all hatch, take the fake egg out and let her sit on it again, repeat seven times, after which the herbal mixture will acquire the tonic quality of authentic ginseng.
A similar method of artificial fashioning (
rengong zhizao

) came from another friend. This involved tricking wild cranes to hatch cooked eggs, repeating the process three times, and using the eggshell as a drinking vessel, which allegedly carried various health benefits. According to Zhao, this rare object could command a very high price at the local market.
In both cases, it was believed that intimate contact with the mother bird’s body would imbue the bitter and dead substance with miraculous efficacy.

是什么驱使一个人花千金买这样的秘方？与猎捕故事一样，方法中繁复的程序与欺骗，构成了最终成品市场价值的重要方面。这些复杂过程，与当时药师虔诚复现古方、不惜工费的誓言相互呼应。但事实上，正是这些额外的劳作抬高了成品的市场价值。换言之，劳动与心力能把死物变成黄金。

What might have driven someone to buy such a recipe for a thousand taels of silver? Like hunting stories, the elaborate procedures and deceptions that went into the methods constituted an important aspect of the market value of the end result. The complex processes resonated with contemporary pharmacists’ pledge to piously reproduce ancient recipes without sparing material expense or labor. But it was, in fact, all this additional labor that inflated the end product’s market value. In other words, labor and effort could transform dead matter into gold.
帝国的纪念品
Souvenirs of Empire

1788年（乾隆五十三年），赵学敏收到儿子寄来的一个包裹；儿子也在遥远的四川叙州府做私人幕僚（地图0.2）。信中附有赵学敏索要的一件标本：所谓鸡血藤，一种木本茎干会渗出深红树脂的植物，据说能即刻治愈一切损伤。儿子解释说，此物得自金沙江的土司（tusi）。赵学敏手拿那块干树脂，想起不久前另一件事：一位曾在云南任职的官员给他看过一块鸡血藤，外观相似，内里质地却全然不同。三年后，谜团仍未解开：一位从云南归来的官员又送给赵学敏一块鸡血藤树脂，治疗他的关节疼痛。这一块看上去又与先前两块不同。赵学敏与此前回家探亲的儿子一同察看这些标本，仍无法断定此物真正的形态应当如何。“惜不能亲历其地（qinli qi di），为之细核，附笔于此，以俟后之君子考订焉。”赵学敏写道。

In 1788 (Qianlong 53), Zhao Xuemin received a package from his son, who also worked as a private secretary in faraway Xuzhou Prefecture (map 0.2). Enclosed in the letter was a specimen that Zhao had requested: the so-called Chicken Blood Vine (
jixueteng
), a plant whose woody stalk oozed crimson-red resin reportedly curing any injuries immediately. His son explained that he had obtained the plant from the indigenous ruler (
tusi

) of the Jinsha River. Holding the piece of dried resin in his hand, Zhao recalled another recent occasion where an official, who had once served in Yunnan, showed him a piece of Chicken Blood Vine: it was similar in appearance but with an altogether different texture inside. The riddle was still not resolved three years later, when an official returning from Yunnan gave Zhao another piece of Chicken Blood Vine resin to treat his joint pain. This one looked still different from the previous two samples. After examining the samples with his son, who was visiting home at the time, Zhao could not reach a conclusion over what the true appearance of the plant should look like. “If only I could be there myself (
qinli qi di
),” Zhao noted with some frustration, “and check on these things carefully!”

清代皇帝及其大臣，并不是唯一能在边疆事务上主张权威、传播新知识的人。在中层任职的边疆官员回乡后会写游记与回忆录；他们的幕僚与技术助手也是如此。除了重复官方宣传清朝治下文明裨益的套话，这些文字还记录了通过礼物交换与实物消费而展开的漫长文化驯化过程。赵学敏托儿子在西南边疆打听的多种鸡血藤标本，对许多来自内地的访客而言，实质上就是边疆经历的纪念品。一位归客告诉赵学敏，驻守腾越的士兵——腾越紧邻清缅边境，是战略要地——常深入山谷采集这种深红树脂，用来送礼或卖给商人。
赵学敏又从一位曾旅居西陲的府同知那里得知，巴里坤（Balikun）的深山中生长着一种无叶植物，那里是哈萨克人居住之地。同样，是“牧马兵”认识并采收其茎，把汁液熬成膏，卖给“远方客商”（yuanke）。
官僚成员与其远亲之间的礼物经济，不可避免地推动了边疆产品的商品化。它们进入既有药物供应范围，是十八世纪清帝国扩张的一个意外结果。

Qing emperors and their ministers were not the only ones who could claim authority in frontier matters and spread new knowledge. Middle-tier bureaucrats serving in frontier posts wrote travelogues and memoirs upon returning home; so did their secretaries and technical assistants. Aside from repeating the official lines that touted the benefits of civilization under Qing rule, these writings also documented the extensive process of cultural domestication via gift exchange and consumption of tangible objects. The multiple specimens of Chicken Blood Vine, which Zhao asked his son to inquire about at the southwestern frontier, served essentially as souvenirs of the frontier experience for many visitors from the provinces. One returnee told Zhao Xuemin that soldiers stationed in Tengyue, a strategic location near the Qing-Burmese border, regularly went into deep valleys to harvest the crimson-red resin to use as gifts or sell to dealers.
From a vice-prefect who had sojourned in the Western border territories (
xichui
), Zhao learned about a leafless plant growing in the deep mountains of Barköl (
Balikun
), where the Kazakhs lived. Again, it was the “horse-herding soldiers” who knew and harvested the stalks, reduced the juice into a paste, and sold it to “guest merchants from afar” (
yuanke

The gift economy between members of the bureaucracy and their extended kin inevitably fueled the commodification of frontier products. Their additions to the existing range of pharmaceutical offerings were an unintended consequence of Qing imperial expansion throughout the eighteenth century.
十八世纪边疆新产品涌入中原时，关于其用途的学界共识尚未形成，更谈不上规范管理。这些异域药物离开原生环境，为缓解熟悉的病痛带来新的希望。其中一种主要的治疗挪用，透露出对幼童天花这一致命祸患的深层焦虑。例如，藏香被郑重宣传为有幼儿家庭的预防措施。赵学敏对这种想法是否可靠表示怀疑，却仍向一位曾在曹寅（1658—1712）手下做事的老者讨要这种昂贵藏香的配方；曹寅是康熙帝有权势的包衣近臣。
另一种获得抗痘名声的边疆产品，是所谓“神黄豆”，来自云南与四川。据赵学敏描述，干豆在敲击或摇动豆荚时会发出悦耳声响。一位访客曾给他看过来自云南的样品。流行验方要求把豆半生半熟地炮制，与芫荽水一同服下：此药消散“痘毒”有奇效。若及早开始服用，孩子甚至可能完全免于天花的折磨。
通过传播这些诉诸新药“神”力的验方，赵学敏实际上承认了其效力的幽秘性质——这种效力部分源自它们在帝国最新边疆的异域出身。

The influx of new frontier products to central China during the eighteenth century took place before any learned consensus over their uses could be consolidated, let alone regulated. Taken from their native habitats, the exotic cures offered new promise for alleviating familiar maladies. One predominant therapeutic appropriation revealed a deep-seated anxiety over the deadly scourge of smallpox among young children. Tibetan incense, for instance, was promoted in earnest as a preventive measure for households with young children. Zhao expressed some doubt about the soundness of the idea, yet nevertheless asked for the recipe for the expensive incense from an old man who once worked for Cao Yin (1658–1712), the powerful bondservant and confidant of the Kangxi emperor.

Another frontier product that acquired anti-pox fame was the so-called Divine Yellow Beans, brought in from Yunnan and Sichuan. According to Zhao’s description, the dried beans produced a pleasant sound when one tapped or shook the pod. A visitor once showed him a sample from Yunnan. A popular recipe dictated that the beans should be prepared half-raw and half-baked, and consumed together with cilantro water: the cure worked wonders for dissipating the “pox poison.” If one started the regimen early enough, a child might even be spared from going through the ordeal of smallpox altogether.
By passing on remedies that invoked the “divine” (
shen
) power of the novel cures, Zhao Xuemin effectively acknowledged the occult nature of their efficacy that, in part, derived from their exotic origins in the empire’s latest frontier.
异域的多重层次
Layers of Foreignness
尽管赵学敏屡屡引用方以智的著作，他却在白胡椒的真面目上与这位大学者略有分歧。方以智记载，广舶胡椒中有一种“玉椒”，色白而味比其他胡椒更辛辣。一百年后，《拾遗》称，白胡椒在宁波的“洋货店”（yanghuodian）里“颇多”；宁波是海上贸易的重要港口。此外，一位商人朋友从外国生意伙伴那里得知，白胡椒是去掉胡椒外皮后再晒干果实制成的，因此本质上与黑胡椒同种（zhong）。
赵学敏虽未直接与外国人做生意，但白胡椒之类的外国商品对他而言触手可及，也是他极感兴趣的对象。他期待从“粤澳洋舶”（Yue Ao yangbo）上“带来”（dailai）异域而令人兴奋的产品，如精油、安息香与龙涎香。
1800年，另一位家人从粤东给他带来一些金鸡纳树枝，并教他一则“澳番”（Ao fan）传下的方子：用金鸡纳与肉桂煎汤，可治各种疟疾。

yanghuodian

) in Ningbo, a major port of maritime trade. Moreover, a merchant friend had learned from his foreign business partners that white peppers were prepared by removing the skin of the peppercorns before sun-drying the fruits and therefore were of essentially the same kind (
zhong

dailai
) from “foreign ships in Canton and Macau” (
Yue Ao yangbo
), such as essential oils, benzoin resin (
anxi xiang
), and ambergris (
longxian xiang

赵学敏在《拾遗》中运用了一套复杂而细腻的词汇来描述外国与异域性。他沿用早期地理文献中的“西洋”与“东洋”等地理术语。同时，他又频繁用“洋”字描述与海上贸易相关的物品。停泊广州、澳门的商船是“洋舶”，宁波经营进口货的中国杂货店是“洋货店”。凡“洋”之物，都在他的消费范围之内，例如他提到“洋画”“洋布”与“洋糖”（按外国新法精制的糖）。在《拾遗》中，赵学敏转录《同寿录》制橙饼的方子：橙子经浸泡、煮软，拌上“洁白洋糖”并反复晒制，这种美味可助消化、化痰。
总体而言，“洋”的异域属性被呈现为无威胁、甚至正面的，尽管仍算得上有点稀罕的享受。

Zhao Xuemin deployed a complex and nuanced terminology in
Shiyi
to describe foreigners and foreignness. He continued to use the geographical terms “Western Seas” (
xiyang
) and “Eastern Seas” (
dongyang

) seen in earlier geographical literature. Meanwhile, he frequently used the term “yang” to describe objects associated with maritime trade. Business vessels docking in Canton and Macau were “foreign ships” (
yangbo
), and Chinese-run groceries that carried imported goods in Ningbo were “foreign goods shops” (
yanghuodian
). Things that were yang were well within his range of consumption, as exemplified by his mention of “foreign painting” (
yanghua
), “foreign cloth” (

; refined sugar prepared according to foreign/new methods). In
Shiyi

Overall, the attribute of yang foreignness was presented as nonthreatening and even positive, if still a somewhat rare treat.

然而，“番”这个称谓呈现的是另一种异己性。它指的是居住在离本土更近的地区的人，尤其是远南一带，如前面提到的“澳番”。在清代官方用语中，“番”也常用来指名义上归清朝统治、却保持自身习俗的原住民族。自1683年清军征服台湾以来，当地“生番/熟番”的区分，成为这些词语传播的重要语境。“西番”一词早已用来指称藏族文化地区，入清以后仍在使用，同时“藏”或“西藏”这一现代称谓也日益通行。在《拾遗》中，赵学敏对藏地喇嘛表现出浓厚兴趣；这些精英僧侣住在北京，为清廷举行法事。1792年，赵学敏得到“数十粒”玛尼丸，这是一种经僧侣加持的药物，据说可作万灵药。他把从亲友处得到的药丸贮在玻璃盆中，并记下早先听到的说法：有人用藏红花“饲”这些药丸，使它们繁生。他还听到生动的故事：北京的喇嘛聚集诵经加持药丸，而药丸竟能像活物一样行动——大丸可以自行分裂、生出小丸，或在空中飞舞。这种药丸是清代贵族与高官的流行礼物，也进入了南方寻常人家。据金御乘讲述，赵学敏得知当地一个聋人只服了三粒玛尼丸便奇迹般恢复听觉，却在妓家过了一夜后又重新失聪。
通过这些关于自行用药的告诫故事，来自西藏的奇物进入了盛清江南的家庭道德想象。

Aofan

In 1792, Zhao Xuemin obtained “several dozen” mani pills, a remedy that had been blessed by the monks and reportedly could be used as a panacea. From family and friends, Zhao received detailed instruction on the storage (in glassware) of those pills and their upkeep (“feed” the pills with Tibetan saffron). He also heard vivid stories of the ritual during which the lamas in Beijing had gathered to pray and bless the pills, which could behave as if they were alive: larger pills could procreate by self-division and generate smaller ones, or fly around in the air. A popular gift for Qing aristocrats and high officials, the pills also found their way into ordinary households in the south. According to a tale told by an itinerant physician, Zhao learned that a local deaf man had miraculously regained his hearing by taking just three mani pills, only to lose it again after spending a night at a prostitute’s home.
Through such cautionary stories of self-medication, strange objects from Tibet found a place in the domestic moral imagination of High Qing Jiangnan.

同样，“番”字被用于给辣椒（fanjiao）、花生（fandou，“番豆”）

The more predominant usage of “fan” in this text, however, extended to objects associated with lands and peoples in and beyond the South China Sea and closely connected to home by the junk trade. For instance, when referred to as
fanbo
, business vessels were related to Batavia (Sunda Kalapa,

Through Zhao Xuemin’s carefully gathered quotes and stories, we see how the category of fan mediated the long process of introducing and domesticating new crops that came into China via Southeast Asia throughout the seventeenth century, from as far away as America. A seventeenth-century source first documented “foreign bananas” (
fanjiao
) that reportedly came from the Ryukyu Kingdom.
Similarly, the term “fan” was applied to the naming of chili pepper (
fanjiao
), peanuts (
fandou
, “foreign bean”),
and sweet potato (
fanshu
, “foreign yam”).
Plants that were unique to Taiwan presented themselves as “foreign/indigenous garlic” (
fansuan
) and “foreign/indigenous ginger” (
fanjiang

Here, the image of the indigene plant overlapped with the image of the indigene person, slowly being transformed into part of the familiar spheres of Qing rule. Fan was, for Zhao Xuemin, foreign in a nonthreatening, even mysterious way.

清初官方汇编则用“夷方”指云南边远边疆。
然而，贬义的“夷”在《拾遗》中出现（28次）远少于较为正面或中性的“洋”（95次）与“番”（79次）；赵学敏以第一人称叙述的自撰按语中，几乎从不使用“夷”。与他引用的许多作者不同，他似乎觉得这个词对自己的目的既无特别用处，也不甚相关。在我看来，这种态度与清代官方文书把“夷”用作“超级符号”的普遍做法形成鲜明对照——那种用法为十九世纪的外交政策定下了基调。
清朝官员坚持使用贬称“夷”，也是一种面向国内受众的政治表态；这些受众很可能像赵学敏一样，早已习惯了洋货或番货作为生活中的熟悉存在。
Lastly, the term

Woyi

Early Qing governmental compendia referred to “barbarian territory” (

Unlike many of the authors he quoted, it seems that he found the term neither particularly useful nor relevant for his purposes. This attitude, in my mind, poses a stark contrast with the prevalent use of “yi” as a “super sign” in Qing governmental documents that set the tone for foreign policy in the nineteenth century.

The Qing official insistence on using the denigrating term “yi” was also a political statement aimed at a domestic audience who, like Zhao Xuemin, might very well have become used to foreign things—yang or fan—as a familiar presence in their life.
那么，从药师的视角看，中国之物与外国之物之间并不存在先验的二元区分。异域不仅以各种称谓和不同程度的陌生感存在，贸易过程本身也会产生具有药效的意外之物。最极端的临时挪用例子，仍发生在外国船只停泊的广州湾。清朝官员查验完毕、货物卸下并存入中国商人经营的商馆之后，本地人会到船上采集所谓“洋船璞”——生于船底龙骨间、形如菌蕈之物。据本地验方，此物是治胃痛的良药。
在另一条目中，赵学敏记载，来自马六甲的船上备有一种特殊火把，用当地所产的可燃树脂制成。中国本地医者会寻找火把上未燃尽的残脂，称之为“番打马”。他们把它研成粉末，与汞混合，制成一种治疗梅毒的流行药膏。
欧洲人生产并运来中国的铁丝，抵达广州时通常已经生锈；人们仔细刮下锈层，用来治疗皮肤疮疡。
来自广州、澳门的燧石被归为“红毛国”所产；番人（fanren）卖走石芯后，外层“白如粉”的石皮便任人取走，成为治疗小伤口的流行药物。
这类奇妙之物，在某种意义上正是对外贸易本身的副产品。它们的吸引力所表达的，并非人们通常以为的中国排外心理，而是一种持久不衰的、对远方交流的民间兴趣。

From a pharmacist’s perspective, then, there was no a priori, binary distinction between Chinese things and foreign things. Not only did the foreign exist in various terminologies and shades of strangeness, the processes of trade themselves yielded unexpected products that possessed medicinal efficacy. The most extreme examples of impromptu appropriation took place again in the Canton Bay, where foreign ships docked. After inspections were performed by Qing officials, and the merchandise was unloaded and stored at one of the Chinese-run factories, locals came to the ships to harvest the so-called Foreign Ship Membrane (
yangchuanpu
), a type of algae attached to the protruding keel of the vessel. According to local recipes, the substance made an excellent remedy for stomach pain.

In another entry, Zhao documented that ships coming from Malacca were equipped with a special kind of torch made with an ignitable resin produced there. Local Chinese healers sought out the unburned remainder resin from the torches, calling it “foreign horse whip” (
fan da ma
). They would grind it into powder, mix it with mercury, and prepare an ointment that became a popular remedy against syphilis.
Iron wires that Europeans produced and brought to China were usually rusted when they reached Canton; the oxidized rust was carefully scraped off to treat skin sores.
Flint stones sourced from Canton and Macau were attributed to the “Red-Haired Nations” (
Hongmao guo
), and after the foreigners (
fanren
) sold the inner cores, the “white, chalky” skin of the stones was removed and given away for free, becoming a popular remedy for minor wounds.

Such wondrous creations were, in a sense, by-products of foreign trade itself. Their attraction expressed not the commonly supposed Chinese xenophobia, but an abiding popular interest in exchanges with afar.

归根结底，“洋虫”风潮之所以可能，恰恰在于在家中饲养小生灵这种开放无尽的乐趣。主人把盒子放在膝上，夜里睡在它旁边，以自身的元气与人的气息（renqi）涵养其药力。可以想见，这既可能是一种昂贵的消遣，也可能是一种相对容易负担的爱好，取决于主人愿意在养护上投入多少。可以说，“洋虫”所谓的药效，并非植根于对其本性的任何宇宙论思辨，而在于人与虫之间朝夕相处、悉心培养的相通；虫子成了一个元气储蓄所，日后可以把元气返还自身。在这里，阴阳五行的繁复关联宇宙论并不适用；重要的只是喂养与被喂养的业力链条，一股无休止的、搏动着的赤裸生命之流。

In the end, the possibility of a “foreign beetle” craze lay precisely in the open-ended pleasure of raising a little creature at home. By keeping the box in his lap and sleeping by it at night, the owner of the strange and tiny pets cultivated their curative power by imparting his own vitality and human breath (
renqi

). One could imagine it to be either an expensive pastime or a relatively accessible hobby, depending on how much one decided to invest in its upkeep. Arguably, the alleged medicinal efficacy of the “foreign beetle” was not rooted in any cosmological speculation about its nature, but rather in the amount of time and care spent cultivating the communion between oneself and the beetle, which served as a depository of vitality that could later be returned to the self. Here the intricate correlative cosmology of yin/yang and the five phases did not apply; all that mattered was the karmic chain of feeding and being fed, an endless stream of pulsating, bare life.
未知的威胁
Threats of the Unknown
洋虫的突然流行，也可能是一种替代现象：此前服用“人药”的风尚已经失宠。清代法律视任何毁伤尸体为非法，处以最严厉的刑罚。赵学敏在十八世纪写作时，觉得以人体部位入药令人厌恶，于是把此前所有本草都有的“人”部整个删去。
然而，法律未能阻止另一种对人体拜物式的迷恋延续下去；这种迷恋并不系于人体本身的性质，而系于它作为接受与传递人之元气的媒介。这些做法都涉及与死尸的接近。

The sudden popularity of foreign beetles may also have been a kind of substitute phenomenon, as the earlier fad of consuming “human drugs” had fallen out of favor. Qing laws deemed any mutilation of corpses to be illegal and punishable by the severest sentences. Writing in the eighteenth century, Zhao Xuemin found the use of human body parts as medicine so repelling that he eliminated “humans” as a category of medicine that had been present in all previous bencao.
Yet the law did not prevent the continuation of another kind of fetishistic fascination with the human body that hinged not on its own nature but on its existence as a
medium
for receiving and imparting human vitality. These practices involved proximity to dead bodies.
《拾遗》记载的一个例子，涉及北方在无漆可用时习惯用来封棺的松香与蜡。迁坟改葬时，人们挖出腐朽的棺材，土人（turen）会刮下松香与蜡，制成敷治伤口的膏药。据赵学敏说，此物之所以珍贵，是因为其中含有“血肉余气”。
赵学敏还引用当代资料与一位老仆的目击证词，描述“人蚜”（renya）的非法交易——这是一种以尸体为食的小虫，由殡葬人通过在棺上钻孔取出。这些虫子由死者散逸的元气“蒸为人蚜”，随后被“方术家”（fangshu jia）与民间医者用来治疗在官府审讯中受刑之人的创伤。可以想象一种围绕监狱运转的阴森经济：死囚的残余元气经由这些虫子转移，用来医治其他囚犯被拷打的身体。

)—small insects that fed on corpses and were collected by mortuary keepers who drilled holes in coffins and retrieved them. The worms, “steamed into existence” from the dissipated vital energy of the dead, were then used by “magicians” (
fangshu jia

) and folk healers to treat wounds of those who had been beaten during official trials. One could imagine a macabre economy revolving around a prison—the remnant vitality of executed convicts transferred, through those insects, to heal the tortured and battered bodies of other inmates.
The functioning of law and order was sustained through the dark efficacy of magic healing.

历史学家孔飞力（Philip A. Kuhn）在记述1769年清代中国妖术恐慌的名著中，思考了这样一个怪诞故事：术士从背后偷袭行人，割去他们的辫发，窃走其灵魂。孔飞力利用清廷为搜捕这些神出鬼没的术士而竭尽全力产生的档案，指出曾有一段时间，王公与农民同样畏惧“未知之人与未见之力”的威胁。

然而，即便没有这类非常事件所激起的大规模歇斯底里，清代日常生活的肌理若没有幽冥之物的存在，难道不是难以想象的吗？孔飞力在书中讨论了木匠与营造匠人所施的符咒仪式；这些人因被认为具有超自然能力而受到怀疑。然而，在更普遍的层面上，异域商品那种无法解释却又广为接受的药效，揭示了清代心灵中更深层的脆弱。在太平年月，好奇心带来繁荣；在动荡年月，正统的虔敬却可能转化为异端的悖乱。如果像赵学敏这样的人都能接受人蚜作为奇药的可能性，那么他离受术士蛊惑也就相去不远了。

In his memorable account of Qing China’s sorcery scare in 1769, historian Philip A. Kuhn pondered the strange tale of sorcerers sneaking up behind people to cut their queued hair and steal their souls. Using archival documents generated from the Qing state’s herculean effort to locate and persecute the elusive sorcerers, Kuhn noted how, for a while, princes and peasants alike all dreaded the threats from “persons unknown and forces unseen.”

Yet even without the mass hysteria fueled by such extraordinary events, was it not the case that the everyday fabric of Qing lives would have been unimaginable without the presence of the occult? In his book, Kuhn discusses the charms and rituals performed by carpenters and builders who came under suspicion due to their perceived supernatural powers. On a more general level, however, the inexplicable—yet widely accepted—pharmaceutical efficacy of exotic commodities revealed a deeper-seated vulnerability in the Qing psyche. In good times, curiosity begat prosperity; but in bad times, orthodox piety could transform into heterodox sedition. If someone like Zhao Xuemin accepted the plausibility of human aphids as a miraculous medicine, he already came quite close to falling under the influence of sorcerers.

清代中国药学商品化的显著成功，也因此对统治者构成一种“看不见的威胁”：他们握有强大的购买力，却不真正知道自己的药物从何而来。跨区域贸易网络很容易被用来传播政治颠覆信息。例如，药师在1750年代臭名昭著的“伪稿案”中扮演了关键角色。1751年，一份充满诽谤、批评乾隆帝的伪奏稿，在偏远的贵州驿站被发现。此案预示了十八年后叫魂案的模式：乾隆帝震怒，命各省官员追查元凶，结果却陷于平行调查与虚假指控的迷宫。贵州官员锁定一名叫谭永福的小商人，他携带伪稿，正从四川前往云南贩卖药材黄连。信息东传之后，邻省最终追查到谭永福所携伪稿的来源，是江西一家名为“天一堂”的药铺，很可能与樟树“药码头”有关。案件以江西一名前武官被定罪处决告终，据称他就是伪稿的作者。
若没有药师广泛的跨区域网络，诽谤材料不可能如此迅速地传播到西南各省。然而，即便在权力鼎盛之时，乾隆帝仍然无法监控商人的思想与行为，尽管他在审查帝国读书人的政治言论方面已无所不用其极。

The remarkable success of the commodification of pharmacy in Qing China thus also posed an “unseen threat” to the rulers, who wielded great purchasing power but did not really know where their remedies came from. The transregional network of trade could easily be appropriated to spread politically subversive messages. Pharmacists, for example, played a crucial role in the notorious “bogus memorial” case in the 1750s. A fake memorial, full of slanderous criticism of the Qianlong emperor, was discovered at a courier station in remote Guizhou in 1751. Presaging the pattern of the soulstealer case eighteen years later, the Qianlong emperor furiously directed his provincial officials to hunt down the culprit, only to get lost in a labyrinth of parallel investigations and fake accusations. Officials in Guizhou homed in on a small-time trader named Tan Yongfu, who had carried the bogus memorial while traveling from Sichuan to Yunnan to sell the medicinal herb Golden Thread. Relaying the information back east, neighboring provinces eventually traced Tan’s source to a pharmacy shop named Tianyitang in Jiangxi, likely with connections to the “medicinal wharf” of Zhangshu. The case was brought to a close after the conviction and execution of a former military officer in Jiangxi, who had allegedly authored the bogus memorial.

Without the extensive interregional network of pharmaceutical merchants, the slanderous material could not have spread so quickly to the southwest provinces. And yet even at the height of his power, the Qianlong emperor remained incapable of monitoring the merchants’ minds and deeds, even though he had gone to unprecedented lengths in censoring political speech among the educated men of the empire.
处于药学行业最底层的个人，往往通过吹嘘自己能获得强效药物、掌握半巫术的力量，来博取利益；他们没什么可失去，却可能大有所获。在十八世纪与十九世纪初，治病救人常被视为吸引人们加入异端教门的最有效手段之一。这些隐秘团体的首领，常靠施行治病仪式来获取信任，手段包括茶叶、按摩、打坐，有时还有真正的药物。
有一次，这样一位首领的过分野心与皇帝本人发生了直接冲突。1779年（乾隆四十四年），皇帝的车驾从北京城外祭谒清室祖陵后回銮，一个年轻人出现在路旁，呈上一封充满疯癫预言的奏书，预言本朝国祚不过五十七年，实质上是在预告乾隆的死期。送信人是一个名叫张九霄的文盲，一生做雇工（yonggong）；他供称自己只是替另一个叫智天豹的人送信。智天豹也随即被捕，受到严加审讯。

Individuals constituting the very lowest strata of the pharmaceutical trade had little to lose and much to gain by playing up their access to potent substances and wielding semimagical powers. Healing was frequently cited as among the single most attractive means of recruitment for heterodox religious sects in the eighteenth and early nineteenth centuries. The leaders of these shadowy groups often gained credibility by performing healing rituals using a range of methods including tea leaves, massage, meditation, and, in some cases, actual medications.

On one occasion, the outsized ambitions of such a leader came into direct conflict with the imperial presence. In 1779 (Qianlong 44), the emperor’s retinue was returning from a visit to the Qing ancestral tombs outside Beijing when a young man showed up by the side of the road and presented a letter full of lunatic prophecies that predicted the current reign to last no more than fifty-seven years, essentially foreboding Qianlong’s death date. The letter-bearer, an illiterate man named Zhang Jiuxiao who had worked all his life as a hired laborer (
yonggong
), confessed that he was merely delivering the letter on behalf of another man named Zhi Tianbao, who was also promptly arrested and rigorously interrogated.

智天豹原来是祁州（地图0.2）开业的一名药师；当时，一个集中化的药材市场正在那里形成。同仁堂等北京大药铺每年都在祁州庙会上采购；到十九世纪，祁州庙会将与樟树齐名。智天豹时运不济，失去了店铺，只能每逢庙会才到祁州，摆摊卖药膏糊口。生计难以维持，他便在附近各县游走，居无定所，最终编造出一套星象预言，借此聚集了一小群追随者。值得注意的是，智天豹与雇工张九霄被捕时都已成家，说明这个小教门对首领而言尚能维持。审讯中，智天豹供称，他希望通过声称与已故雍正帝神灵相通，换取富贵。官府搜查其家，只找到一些破旧（jiupo）的医书与星象书，大概是智天豹从父亲那里继承的。

Zhi Tianbao turned out to be a former pharmacist practicing in Qizhou (map 0.2), where a centralized medicinal marketplace was taking shape around that time. The great pharmacies of Beijing, such as Tongrentang, made purchases in Qizhou at the annual market fair, which would eventually rival the stature of Zhangshu during the nineteenth century. Due to bad fortune, Zhi had lost his shop and made a living instead by coming to Qizhou only during the market fairs, setting up a stand selling medicinal poultices. Unable to make ends meet, he traveled around nearby counties with no stable home, and eventually conjured up an astrological prophecy that enabled him to gather a small group of followers. Notably, both Zhi and laborer Zhang were married at the times of their arrest, indicating that the tiny sect was doing well enough for the leaders. During his interrogation, Zhi confessed that he had hoped that by claiming spiritual communication with the deceased emperor Yongzheng, he would receive wealth and status (
fugui
) in return. Authorities searched his home, only to find some old and tattered (
jiupo
) books on medicine and astrology, which Zhe likely inherited from his father.
说来奇怪，乾隆帝似乎相信智天豹预言中的某些成分。官员建议处以极刑——凌迟——皇帝却写下长篇谕旨，认真回应智天豹关于其统治终期的预言，说自己若能在位五十七年，其实已很满足。但他仍对智天豹妄称与先帝神灵相通而感到冒犯。最终，智天豹被立即斩首（被认为比凌迟从轻）。官方邸报以一则简短报道总结全案，并赞颂皇帝的明察。
在这个案子里，我们再次看到皇帝与穷药师共同怀有的对神异预言的信仰。乾隆并不怀疑灵媒的存在；他只是不能容忍除自己之外的人声称能通达祖先的灵魂。
Strangely enough, the Qianlong emperor seemed to believe some elements of Zhi’s prognostication. When officials recommended the most severe punishment—death by a thousand cuts (
lingchi

)—the emperor wrote a lengthy response that seriously engaged with Zhi Tianbao’s prophecy of the end date of his rule, saying that he would in fact be content enough to reign for as many as fifty-seven years. Yet he still took offense at Zhi’s pretentious claim to have had spiritual contact with his deceased father. In the end, Zhi Tianbao received a death penalty by immediate beheading (considered more lenient than a slow death). The whole case was summarized in a brief report in an official gazette that praised the emperor’s sagacity.

Again, in this case, we see a common belief in miraculous prophecy shared by both the emperor and the poor pharmacist alike. Qianlong did not doubt the existence of spiritual mediums; he merely took offense that anyone
other than himself
might claim access to the souls of his ancestors.

最后一个集中体现药材贸易棘手性质的案例，发生在1791年，距年迈的皇帝在位六十年后禅位仅有数年。乾隆审阅福州将军魁伦关于琉球船只出口免税的奏折时，注意到所列货物包括药用大黄（dahuang），以及“洋参”、苏木（sumu）等外洋（waiyang）商品。数年前，乾隆为惩罚不驯的俄国人，曾暂时关闭恰克图（地图0.2）的边境贸易站，并对大黄实施禁运；俄国人似乎离不开这种商品。（实际上，俄国人只是把中国大黄转销欧洲市场的中介。）南方的广州口岸也禁止进口俄国毛皮，以防大黄在对俄交易中被走私出去。因此，琉球请求购买大量大黄，引起了皇帝的警觉：他们会不会是想把大黄转卖回俄国人，以牟取不法之利？

A final case that epitomized the problematic nature of the pharmaceutical trade occurred in 1791, only a few years before the aging emperor abdicated his throne after ruling for sixty years. Reviewing a letter sent from the Ryukyu Kingdom’s envoys, Qianlong noticed that they had requested to purchase a long list of goods, including a large quantity of medicinal rhubarb (
dahuang
) and outer sea (
waiyang
) commodities such as “foreign” ginseng (
yang shen
) and sappanwood (
sumu

). It was several years since Qianlong decided to punish the unruly Russians by temporarily shutting the border trade outpost in Kiakhta (map 0.2) and imposing an embargo on rhubarb, a commodity that the Russians seemed unable to live without. (In reality, the Russians were merely intermediaries supplying Chinese rhubarb to the European market). Imports of Russian fur were also banned at the southern port of Canton, for fear that rhubarb might be smuggled out in transactions with Russians. The large quantity of rhubarb that the Ryukyus requested thus raised alarm for the emperor: Might they have been seeking illicit profit by reselling the rhubarb back to the Russians?
经查，琉球人是在获准居留的福建采购；承买药材的行户供称，各样药材“俱由江西樟树镇贩运来闽销售”，而江西不产大黄，听说陕西泾阳县是大黄“汇集之所”，再转发汉口、樟树等地。琉球国通事魏廷玉称，琉球与西洋、暹罗相距遥远，向来没有商人贸易洋参和苏木，所以就在福建购买；至于大黄，过去每年购买数百斤或数千斤不等，禁令颁行后则按核定数目由官府代买，运回本国，并未转售他处。
接到报告后，乾隆便不再追究此事。

这份报告很好地说明了大黄成为商品的多层过程：药材首先在初级市场（泾阳）成批“成庄”（chengzhuang），再经水路顺流运至樟树，西北所产的大黄在那里被重新分配给来自全国各地的商人。清中国（通过广州）在市场交换中的地位远高于琉球王国等较小国家，因此西洋参、苏木等洋货能卖到最好的价钱。欧洲、美国与暹罗商人不仅购买中国制造的商品，也参与向清中国供应消费品，从而把自己的经营与往来樟树、祁州的国内药材批发商联结起来。国内跨区域贸易与海上贸易之间界限的模糊，被清廷及其他参与者都当作现实来对待。
This report nicely illustrates the multilayered process by which rhubarb became a commodity: the plants were first assembled in bulk (
chengzhuang

) at a primary marketplace (Jingyang), then shipped via waterways downstream to Zhangshu, where the northwestern plant was redistributed to traders hailing from all parts of the country. Qing China (through Canton) commanded a much higher place in market exchange than smaller countries, such as the Ryukyu kingdom, and so one could obtain the best price for foreign (
yang

to

Qing China, thus linking their operations with those of domestic pharmaceutical wholesalers frequenting Zhangshu and Qizhou. The blurring of boundaries between domestic interregional and maritime trade was treated as a reality by the Qing state as well as by other players.

乾隆帝关于熟悉之物与异域之物的种种设想，最终被证明是错的。到十九世纪之交，印度次大陆所产鸦片将沿着赵学敏获得异域药物的同一路线进入中国，数量却大得多。1791年，清廷尚不能阻止琉球使节在中国买药；五十年后，他们已几乎无法用法律把鸦片挡在广州水域之外。新组织起来的药学建立在好奇心与商业知识之上，而非官方视域或医学正统，因此对二者都保持不透明。清代药师与消费者所建造的货物世界，将证明比相互竞争的医学理论流派更为坚韧，也比王朝本身延续得更久。

The Qianlong emperor’s assumptions about the familiar and the exotic turned out to be wrong. By the turn of the nineteenth century, opium produced in the subcontinent would enter China via the same routes through which Zhao Xuemin had received his exotica, albeit in much more abundant quantities. In 1791, Qing authorities could not prevent the Ryukyu envoys from buying medicine in China; five decades later, they could hardly use their laws to keep opium out of the waters of Canton. The newly organized medicine was built on curiosity and mercantile knowledge instead of official purview or medical orthodoxy, and hence remained opaque to both. The world of goods built by Qing pharmacists and consumers would prove to be more tenacious than the rivaling schools of medical theory and outlast the dynasty itself.
